title: F. Multiplicative Arrays
statement:
You're given integers k and n. For each integer x from 1 to k, count the number of integer arrays a such that all of the following are satisfied:

Note that two arrays b and c are different if either their lengths are different, or if there exists an index 1 ≤ i ≤ |b| such that b_i≠ c_i.

Output the answer modulo 998,244,353.

The first line contains an integer t (1 ≤ t≤ 10^3) — the number of independent test cases.

The only line of each test case contains two integers k and n (1 ≤ k ≤ 10^5, 1≤ n ≤ 9·10^8).

It is guaranteed that the sum of k over all test cases does not exceed 10^5.

For each test case, output k space-separated integers on a new line: the number of arrays for x=1,2,…,k, modulo 998,244,353.
